newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money soars to 4.00/25 at month-end.
newsitem.headline: German call money soars to 4.00/25 at month-end.

text.p: German call money surged to trade at 4.00/25 percent on Friday as banks raced to complete outstanding reserve obligations before month-end, leaving dealers unsure of how prices may develop this afternoon.
On Thursday rates traded between 3.10/15 percent reaching highs of 3.25 percent as banks were already preparing for month-end which often results in significant price gyrations.

Dealers said they were surprised by the high amount of Lombard borrowings standing at 1.9 billion marks on Thursday after 100 million marks on Wednesday, saying rates had not climbed above 3.25 percent on Thursday.
Today the government was active in the market which helped tighten liquidity and prop up rates , dealers said.
A relatively high monthly average reserve rate however may indicate that rates could come off this afternoon.
The Bundesbank reported that banks held 44.3 billion marks in non-interest bearing accounts at the Bundesbank on Thursday, up from 43.7 billion marks a day earlier.

Average holdings however dipped to 41.4 billion marks from 43.1 billion marks. The daily Frankfurt Interbank Offered Rate was set at 4.21667 percent on Friday compared with 3.22333 percent. --Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525
